root_cause.escaped_defect: Repository Janitor counted explicitly retired open PRs as active terminal-delivery successors and could auto-reopen an old unmerged terminal lease even when a later same-obligation successor had already merged.
root_cause.evidence: Janitor run 37595314458 attempt 1 failed on #3928 with three retired successors. After manual closure, attempt 2 auto-reopened retired leases and failed again on #3953 with the same ambiguity class. After #4060 merged and removed false retired-successor ambiguity, workflow_dispatch run 37641738149 reached apply-safe cleanup but closed #3945 before validating #3942 -> #3945, proving cleanup ordering itself could invalidate a later action in the same deterministic plan.

prevention.active_successor: Only non-retired open PRs may count as active successors.
prevention.merged_successor: A merged same-obligation successor satisfies the old closed terminal lease and prevents unsafe auto-reopen.
prevention.fail_closed: Multiple genuine non-retired active successors remain a terminal ambiguity and still fail closed.
prevention.stale_actions: Existing normal cancel -> force-cancel -> delete-fallback escalation remains unchanged.
prevention.apply_order: Cleanup actions are applied oldest-first by PR number. Because an explicit successor is necessarily a newer PR, predecessor validation completes before that successor can itself be closed by the same plan.

evidence.proof_boundary: retired successor filtering, merged-successor satisfaction, oldest-first transitive cleanup, and unchanged genuine multi-writer fail-closed behavior
